$comment: §10.7 referral rate table — the policy the treasury's payer follows. `ref: null` is the default row; a row with a name overrides it for that referrer. `bp` is the referrer's share and `rebateBp` the buyer's rebate, both in basis points of the fee in effect at the G's height; a row without `rebateBp` pays no rebate. The row in effect for (ref, height) is the most specific ref among rows with fromHeight ≤ height, latest fromHeight winning. `selfBp` is the rate for BOTH payouts when the buyer already controls the referring name (§7.2 effective sender); a row without one prices that case at each payout's own rate. Rates are stated NET of the §10.2 burn share — the burn base counts only inflows to the treasury, so a gross payout would have the treasury burning on money it never kept; 400 bp is a headline 5% with the 20% burn already deducted. Append rows with a height; never edit one — a recomputation must reproduce every past payout. `netOfBurn` says the row's rates already have the burn taken out, so the app can state the headline they came from (400 bp netOfBurn renders as 5%, and 5% is what Kike published) — it is a label on the rate, never an input to a payout, and adding one to a row changes nothing anybody was paid. The app's docs page renders this file.

rates.note: default — 10% of the fee in effect (decided 2026-09-10); selfBp 0: a buyer who already owns the referring name brought nobody (2026-09-12)

default — the 10% referrer share splits into 5% for the referrer and 5% back to the buyer (Kike, 2026-09-12), each stated net of the 20% burn: 400 bp. 8% of the fee leaves the treasury, which keeps it in exactly the position a burn on a net base would: a referral payout is net of the burn
